builtBy: Research by hand, 2026-11-21: the club records from each club's own website (and the adidas 3SSB program directory); the ties from the players' Prep Hoops pages and articles, their Hudl, SportsRecruits and MaxPreps career pages. Every tie's every source was re-read at assembly; no script rebuilds this file.
notes: The travel (AAU) basketball clubs that players on the 58 boys basketball rosters MaxPreps lists so far are tied to. The linking rule is field hockey's (README, "Clubs"): a public page must name the player and a basketball club or program, and either name the player's high school (with the right city where a school of the name exists elsewhere), or give the roster's class year with a hometown in the school's own area. A name alone never counts, a class year that disagrees with the roster rules a match out (except one a year ahead of a roster grade that is last season's: see data/basketball/rosters-enrichment.json), and social media is never a source.

Club records (13): written from each club's own site, or the adidas 3SSB program directory, for the clubs our players' pages name, the programs the circuits list near the schools, and those met on the way. No public directory lists the boys' travel programs of any area (the Nike EYBL team list is an image, Puma's and others are drawn by script or refuse automated reads), so no area was searched for every club: the Peninsula and the South Bay most, San Francisco, the East Bay and Marin only for clubs a player's page names. No club based in Santa Cruz County was found. No record names a coach.

Ties: 40 for 39 players at 22 schools. Sources: Prep Hoops player pages ("attends <school> ... and plays club basketball for <club>", the school linked to its Prep Hoops team page, whose title gives the city) and the evaluation cards in its articles; Hudl profiles' team lists (on the school's own team); SportsRecruits profiles' club block (read twice through the page's JSON); MaxPreps career pages' club-teams block. Club names are mapped to a record by hand: Esface to Team Esface; SV Soldiers to Silicon Valley Soldiers; Bay City Warriors to Bay City Basketball (its high school boys' program, by the club's own site); Oakland Soldiers E16 EYBL to Oakland Soldiers; San Jose Spartans 300 Elite to San Jose Spartans; NBBA to North Bay Basketball Academy; Hudl's 'Gold Basketball' to Peninsula Gold.

Status. current: a source dated 2026 (a Prep Hoops article's 2026 session roster naming the club team, a Hudl entry reaching 2026, a MaxPreps entry joined or edited in 2026). past: a Hudl entry ending in 2024 or earlier, or a MaxPreps entry last edited before 2025. unknown: everything else, including every Prep Hoops player page (undated; the date shown is the profile's creation). Where sources differ, current is shown before unknown, and unknown before past.

Left out: Serra players' Prep Hoops pages, which say 'Junipero Serra-San Mateo' but link the Gardena school's team page (not the right school); pages giving a school with no city where a namesake exists (a St. Ignatius card with no city; a Willow Glen page placed in Nevada); a Hudl 'AmFb Combine' entry (an event in Lincoln, NE, not a club); club entries for teams before sixth grade; JV players' ties (jvAffiliations is empty).

No record, so no tie shown, although a page ties a rostered player to the club: Team California (2), Seattle Rotary (2), Roadrunners Sports Club (2), Seattle Rotary (EYBL) (2), All In Elite (5), South Bay Snipers (1), San Jose Ninjas (1), Team elite (1), Team Evolution (1), Bay Area Sonics (1), RBA Waves (1), Flight Academy (1), Santa Cruz Premier (1). No club-owned site or circuit directory entry was found for these (All In Elite, Team California, Seattle Rotary and Roadrunners Sports Club are named on Prep Hoops pages; the rest each on one MaxPreps career page).

Every source of every tie was re-read at assembly on 2026-11-21 by a separate script and its quote found on the page as served (Hudl and MaxPreps: the page's own data fields; SportsRecruits: the profile JSON, twice).
